top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a specific, reproduced invention: Katori's magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms in an optical lattice, which removes the trap light shift on the clock transition, and its realisation at the 10^-18 level, with Ye's group taking the strontium clock to record accuracy. Sr, Yb and Hg clocks agree across independent laboratories, so interpretation is stable, and the two names map onto two identifiable contributions. With the citation drawn narrowly around the lattice concept, the overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes is manageable. P002 is a strong but younger case whose pairing mechanism is unsettled and whose three names omit Yuan Cao, first author of the decisive 2018 experiments. It still ranks above no award because the phenomena are real, widely reproduced and field-opening.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for Katori or Ye (P001) or MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero (P002); my profile ties (TEM and microscopy community, IFSM, Chalmers, David Clarke at IBM) do not involve any credited name on this slate.
